newsitem.title: CHINA: China to increase 97 summer grain by 2.5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: China to increase 97 summer grain by 2.5 mln T.

text.p: China's Ministry of Agriculture has set a target to increase its summer grain harvest by 2.5 million tonnes next summer after a bumper crop for 1996, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
Officials have said they expect a total grain harvest of a record 480 million tonnes for this year, up from a record 466 million last year.

The new summer harvest target anticipates the summer grain acreage to reach 31.33 million hectares with per hectare yield growing by 75 kg from 1996 levels, the newspaper said. It did not give comparative figures.
The minimum increase for next summer is set at 1.5 million tonnes, it said.
The 1996 summer grain harvest hit 110 million tonnes, up 3.0 percent from last year.
Output of early rice reached 44 million tonnes, up by 1.8 million tonnes from a year ago.
Rapeseed output is expected to reach 8.8 million tonnes next year despite an anticipated fall in 1996 output, the newspaper said.

The success of the 1997 harvest will hinge on improvement in per-unit wheat yield, the newspaper quoted ministry analysts as saying. The gap between the highest per-hectare yield of wheat and the lowest was 4.74 tonnes in 1995, it said.
Mechanised wheat-sowing acreage will increase by 1.07 million hectares in this autumn and winter season compared with last year, it said.
